edition.name: Migne PL 4 (1844), Ep. LXIV, via Corpus Corporum / Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Cum ergo haec tormenta, haec supplicia in die judicii Dominus comminetur iis qui diabolo obtemperant et idolis sacrificant, quomodo se putat posse agere pro Dei sacerdote qui obtemperavit et servivit diaboli sacerdotibus? aut quomodo putat manum suam transferri posse ad Dei sacrificium et precem Domini quae captiva fuerit sacrilegio et crimini, quando in Scripturis divinis Deus ad sacrificium prohibeat accedere sacerdotes etiam in leviori crimine constitutos, et in Levitico dicat: Homo in quo fuerit vitium et macula non accedet offerre dona Deo. Item in Exodo: Et sacerdotes qui accedunt ad Dominum Deum sanctificentur, ne forte derelinquat illos Dominus. Et iterum: Et cum accedunt ministrare ad altare sancti, non adducent in se delictum, ne moriantur. Qui ergo gravia in se delicta adduxerunt, id est, qui idolis sacrificando sacrilega sacrificia fecerunt, sacerdotium Dei sibi vindicare non possunt, nec ullam in conspectu ejus precem pro fratribus facere, quando in Evangelio scriptum sit: Deus peccatorem non audit; sed si quis Deum coluerit et voluntatem ejus fecerit, illum audit. Quamvis sic quorumdam pectora tenebrarum ingruentium profunda caligo caecaverit, ut de praeceptis salubribus nihil lucis admittant, sed se mel a recto limite veri itineris aversi, per praeceps et per abruptum criminum suorum nocte atque errore rapiantur.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, when the Lord threatens these torments, these punishments on the day of judgment to those who obey the devil and sacrifice to idols, how does the one who obeyed and served the devil's priests think he can act as a priest of God? Or how does he think his hand, which was captive to sacrilege and crime, can be transferred to the sacrifice of God and the prayer of the Lord? Since in the divine Scriptures, God prohibits priests who are even in a lesser crime from approaching the sacrifice, and says in Leviticus: A man in whom there is a defect and a blemish shall not approach to offer gifts to God. Also in Exodus: And the priests who approach the Lord God shall sanctify themselves, lest the Lord abandon them. And again: And when they approach to minister at the holy altar, they shall not bring guilt upon themselves, lest they die. Therefore, those who have brought serious guilt upon themselves, that is, those who have made sacrilegious sacrifices by sacrificing to idols, cannot claim the priesthood of God for themselves, nor can they offer any prayer on behalf of their brothers in His sight, since it is written in the Gospel: God does not hear the sinner; but if someone has worshiped God and done His will, He hears him. Although the deep darkness of approaching shadows has blinded the hearts of some, so that they admit no light from the salutary precepts, but have turned themselves away from the right path of the true journey, and are swept away by the night and error of their crimes through precipice and abruptness.
